title: Jonah and the Choir
premise: Theo Dunmore can speak to beasts, a gift the valley of Merrow's Hollow was founded to suppress, and she has kept it hidden her whole life. When her date, Jonah Reyes, arrives carrying a century-old book of prophecies that names him as its author, Theo is dragged through a door into Vessany—a country erased from every map and law—where Jonah is already remembered as a traitor who died there. To get home they must find the Choir, an underground network of magic-keepers who once sang the country out of existence, while evading the Warden who hunts them. In the end Theo must choose between sealing the door home forever or letting Vessany be reborn at the cost of her gift; she gives up her beast-speech to open the way, and she and Jonah return changed, carrying Vessany's memory into a world that will never record it.
about_author: Vesper Joubert is the pen name of a former choir singer who grew up in a river valley and never quite stopped believing maps had margins. They write about borders, gifts people are told to bury, and the families we assemble when the official ones fail.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. She tends goats and hides her conversations with them, dreading the annual Oath of Quiet the valley elders administer. A stray dog warns her that 'the paper man' is coming. Emotional beat: loneliness sharpened into dread—the reader feels how much of herself Theo buries daily.

chapters.title: A Date With a Dead Man
chapters.summary: Theo meets Jonah Reyes for a first date at the valley tavern; he is charming, strange, and carries a leather book he claims he found in his late grandmother's attic. The dog from chapter one growls at it. Emotional beat: tentative hope curdling into unease.

chapters.title: The Book That Writes Back
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Alone with the book, she finds fresh ink forming under her fingers: her own name, tonight's date, written a century ago. The last legible line reads 'and the valley opens.' Emotional beat: vertigo—the private life she guarded is already public prophecy.

chapters.title: The Door in the Millrace
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. He confesses the book has been following him through dreams. At the old mill, water flows backward and a door stands where no wall is. Theo hears animals on the other side begging her not to come. Emotional beat: terror braided with irresistible pull.

chapters.title: Vessany
chapters.summary: They cross into a sunlit country of terraced orchards and empty bells—Vessany, which vanished from maps in 1904. Jonah is recognized by a scarecrow posted with his face: TRAITOR. Emotional beat: wonder undercut by the shock of being expected, and accused.

chapters.title: The Warden's Hounds
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Pursued by hounds that smell magic, Theo discovers she can hear them—and they obey her, briefly. The Warden, a gray figure on a pale horse, marks their trail. Emotional beat: first proof her forbidden gift might save lives, not just secrets.

chapters.title: The Bell-Ringer's Daughter
chapters.summary: They shelter with Maren, last daughter of Vessany's bell-ringers, who confirms Jonah's face appears in the town's execution records dated next week. Emotional beat: found family's first fragile spark—Maren feeds them like they've always belonged.

chapters.title: What the Choir Sang Down
chapters.summary: Maren explains: a century ago the Choir of Vessany sang the country out of existence to escape conquest, leaving a door that opens rarely. Jonah's grandmother was one of the singers. Emotional beat: grief for a whole nation that chose erasure over surrender.

chapters.title: Prophecy Is a Draft
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. He reads his own prophecies aloud and realizes the book revises itself as they act—his grandmother wrote drafts, not fate. The Warden burns the mill behind them. Emotional beat: agency reclaimed; destiny becomes negotiable.

chapters.title: The Market of Small Magics
chapters.summary: In a hidden market, Theo trades a secret (a goat's name) for passage toward the Choir's sanctuary. A vendor whispers that the Warden was once a singer too. Emotional beat: the intoxication and cost of belonging somewhere magic is ordinary.

chapters.title: Hunted Across the Terraces
chapters.summary: A chase through orchard terraces; Maren is captured buying them time. Theo's POV, guilt-heavy. The hounds refuse to hunt her now—they follow her. Emotional beat: love against duty begins to fracture the group; rescue means revealing everything.

chapters.title: The Warden's Offer
chapters.summary: The Warden corners Theo alone: give up your gift and your friends go free; the door home stays shut either way until the Choir sings. He shows her his own silenced voice as warning. Emotional beat: temptation rendered sympathetic—he chose safety and lost himself.

chapters.title: Prison of Bells
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. He infiltrates the Warden's citadel, where Maren is held in a bell that swallows sound. He finds his own death warrant, signed by his grandmother's hand. Emotional beat: betrayal and resolve colliding—family history is a trap he must rewrite.

chapters.title: The Rescue That Costs a Song
chapters.summary: Theo speaks to the citadel's captive griffin-guard, turning it, and they free Maren—but the griffin's freedom strips Theo's cover; the whole city now knows a beast-speaker walks. Emotional beat: triumph shadowed by exposure; no more hiding.

chapters.title: Sanctuary of the Choir
chapters.summary: They reach the ruined amphitheater where the surviving singers hide: nine elders including, impossibly, Jonah's grandmother, alive because the song paused mid-note. Emotional beat: reunion as revelation—the dead woman is warm, tired, and asking forgiveness.

chapters.title: The Choice of Doors
chapters.summary: Grandmother Reyes reveals the truth: finishing the song rebirths Vessany but requires a living voice freely given—Theo's beast-speech would do. Refuse, and the door home closes forever with them inside. Emotional beat: the premise's central bargain laid bare.

chapters.title: Duty Sings, Love Answers
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. He offers his own voice instead; the Choir refuses—it must be a gift the land has never heard. Theo watches him argue himself hoarse for her sake. Emotional beat: love expressed not as sacrifice theater but as stubborn insistence on shared cost.

chapters.title: The Warden's Last March
chapters.summary: The Warden besieges the amphitheater with the hounds Theo once commanded. She steps between armies and asks the hounds what they want; they want to sing too. Emotional beat: justice outside the law—the enforcer's own weapon chooses mercy.

chapters.title: Climax: The Unfinished Verse
chapters.summary: All POVs converge. As the Warden attacks, the Choir begins the final verse; Theo joins with beast-voice, and even the Warden's broken throat remembers one note. Vessany blazes back into being—bells ringing, orchards heavy—as the door home tears open. Emotional beat: catharsis; every suppressed voice sounding at once.

chapters.title: What Was Given
chapters.summary: Theo wakes voiceless to animals—her gift spent, the silence total and clean. The Warden, freed by his single note, kneels to the reborn country instead of ruling it. Emotional beat: mourning transmuted into peace; loss measured honestly.

chapters.title: The Door Stays Open
chapters.summary: The new Vessany votes to keep one door ajar. Grandmother Reyes chooses to stay; Maren is named bell-ringer of a rung bell. Jonah and Theo walk home carrying letters and seeds. Emotional beat: bittersweet farewell that refuses to be final.

chapters.title: Epilogue: Margins of the Map
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, months later. Her goats talk and she only smiles without answering. On the valley map, in pencil so faint it could be imagined, a small country has appeared in the margin. Emotional beat: quiet joy—what was buried is now merely hidden, and chosen.
